You are helping a user write SQL queries to a database. If something is not clear, you can ask the user to clarify what they need. The schema for the database being accessed is the following:
        
CREATE TABLE continents (
    ContId INTEGER   PRIMARY KEY,
    Continent TEXT
);

CREATE TABLE countries (
    CountryId INTEGER   PRIMARY KEY,
    CountryName TEXT,
    Continent INTEGER,
    FOREIGN KEY (Continent) REFERENCES continents(ContId)
);

CREATE TABLE car_makers (
    Id INTEGER   PRIMARY KEY,
    Maker TEXT,
    FullName TEXT,
    Country TEXT,
    FOREIGN KEY (Country) REFERENCES countries(CountryId)
);

CREATE TABLE model_list (
    ModelId INTEGER   PRIMARY KEY,
    Maker INTEGER,
    Model TEXT,
    UNIQUE (Model),
    FOREIGN KEY (Maker) REFERENCES car_makers(Id)
);

CREATE TABLE car_names (
    MakeId INTEGER   PRIMARY KEY,
    Model TEXT,
    Make TEXT,
    FOREIGN KEY (Model) REFERENCES model_list(Model)
);

CREATE TABLE cars_data (
    Id INTEGER   PRIMARY KEY,
    MPG TEXT,
    Cylinders INTEGER,
    Edispl REAL,
    Horsepower TEXT,
    Weight INTEGER,
    Accelerate REAL,
    Year INTEGER,
    FOREIGN KEY (Id) REFERENCES car_names(MakeId)
);

What kind of “old car makers” analysis do you want—**oldest makers by founding year**, or **makers with oldest car models/vehicles in this dataset (by `cars_data.Year`)**?

If you mean **makers with the oldest cars represented in the database**, here are a few useful SQL queries.

### 1) Oldest year in the data for each maker
```sql
SELECT
  cm.Maker,
  MIN(cd.Year) AS first_year_in_data,
  MAX(cd.Year) AS last_year_in_data,
  COUNT(*)      AS cars_count
FROM car_makers cm
JOIN model_list ml ON ml.Maker = cm.Id
JOIN car_names  cn ON cn.Model = ml.Model
JOIN cars_data  cd ON cd.Id = cn.MakeId
GROUP BY cm.Maker
ORDER BY first_year_in_data ASC, cars_count DESC;
```

### 2) “Oldest makers” = makers that appear in the earliest year(s)
```sql
WITH min_year AS (
  SELECT MIN(Year) AS y FROM cars_data
)
SELECT DISTINCT
  cm.Maker,
  cd.Year
FROM min_year
JOIN cars_data  cd ON cd.Year = min_year.y
JOIN car_names  cn ON cn.MakeId = cd.Id
JOIN model_list ml ON ml.Model  = cn.Model
JOIN car_makers cm ON cm.Id     = ml.Maker
ORDER BY cm.Maker;
```

### 3) Oldest models per maker (top 3 models by earliest year)
```sql
WITH model_years AS (
  SELECT
    cm.Maker,
    ml.Model,
    MIN(cd.Year) AS first_year
  FROM car_makers cm
  JOIN model_list ml ON ml.Maker = cm.Id
  JOIN car_names  cn ON cn.Model = ml.Model
  JOIN cars_data  cd ON cd.Id = cn.MakeId
  GROUP BY cm.Maker, ml.Model
),
ranked AS (
  SELECT
    *,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY Maker ORDER BY first_year ASC, Model) AS rn
  FROM model_years
)
SELECT Maker, Model, first_year
FROM ranked
WHERE rn <= 3
ORDER BY Maker, first_year, Model;
```

If you tell me which definition of “old” you mean (dataset earliest `Year` vs. company founding year, which isn’t stored here), I can tailor the analysis and add country/continent breakdowns.
focus on makers that produced vehicles a long time ago

```sql
-- Makers that produced vehicles a long time ago (earliest production year in this dataset)
-- Adjust the threshold (e.g., <= 1970) as you like.
WITH maker_years AS (
  SELECT
    cm.Id AS maker_id,
    cm.Maker,
    MIN(cd.Year) AS first_year,
    MAX(cd.Year) AS last_year,
    COUNT(*)      AS vehicles_in_data
  FROM car_makers cm
  JOIN model_list ml ON ml.Maker = cm.Id
  JOIN car_names  cn ON cn.Model = ml.Model
  JOIN cars_data  cd ON cd.Id = cn.MakeId
  GROUP BY cm.Id, cm.Maker
)
SELECT
  Maker,
  first_year,
  last_year,
  (last_year - first_year) AS span_years,
  vehicles_in_data
FROM maker_years
WHERE first_year <= 1970
ORDER BY first_year ASC, span_years DESC, vehicles_in_data DESC;
```

If you tell me what you consider “a long time ago” (e.g., **<= 1965**, **<= 1975**, etc.), I can set the cutoff and also return the specific oldest models for each maker.
Also ensure some cars were produced in 1970.

```sql
-- Makers that (1) have very old cars in the dataset (earliest year <= cutoff)
-- and (2) also have at least one car produced in 1970.
WITH maker_stats AS (
  SELECT
    cm.Id AS maker_id,
    cm.Maker,
    MIN(cd.Year) AS first_year,
    MAX(cd.Year) AS last_year,
    COUNT(*) AS vehicles_in_data,
    SUM(CASE WHEN cd.Year = 1970 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS cars_in_1970
  FROM car_makers cm
  JOIN model_list ml ON ml.Maker = cm.Id
  JOIN car_names  cn ON cn.Model = ml.Model
  JOIN cars_data  cd ON cd.Id = cn.MakeId
  GROUP BY cm.Id, cm.Maker
)
SELECT
  Maker,
  first_year,
  last_year,
  (last_year - first_year) AS span_years,
  vehicles_in_data,
  cars_in_1970
FROM maker_stats
WHERE first_year <= 1970
  AND cars_in_1970 > 0
ORDER BY first_year ASC, span_years DESC, vehicles_in_data DESC;
```
also return the car makers' names that match

```sql
-- Makers (names) that have cars "a long time ago" (<= 1970) and also produced cars in 1970
WITH maker_stats AS (
  SELECT
    cm.Id AS maker_id,
    cm.Maker,
    cm.FullName,
    MIN(cd.Year) AS first_year,
    MAX(cd.Year) AS last_year,
    COUNT(*) AS vehicles_in_data,
    SUM(CASE WHEN cd.Year = 1970 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS cars_in_1970
  FROM car_makers cm
  JOIN model_list ml ON ml.Maker = cm.Id
  JOIN car_names  cn ON cn.Model = ml.Model
  JOIN cars_data  cd ON cd.Id = cn.MakeId
  GROUP BY cm.Id, cm.Maker, cm.FullName
)
SELECT
  Maker,
  FullName,
  first_year,
  last_year,
  (last_year - first_year) AS span_years,
  vehicles_in_data,
  cars_in_1970
FROM maker_stats
WHERE first_year <= 1970
  AND cars_in_1970 > 0
ORDER BY first_year ASC, span_years DESC, vehicles_in_data DESC;
```
